analysis:
The CHANGELOG units (head lines 871+ and 1323+) are release notes only. The visible entries describe network-stats caching and staleness, profiler and fleet snapshots, and the earlier provider and coordinator releases. They do not change code or trust policy. The 'historical display is never authorization' claim in the network-stats bullets matches the canonical model header and TB-011 and introduces no new claim.

provider-swift/Sources/ProviderCore/Service/LaunchAgent.swift makes two changes.

(1) plistPath()/logPath() (head lines 20-31) now resolve the home directory through LaunchctlControl.homeDirectory() instead of FileManager.default.homeDirectoryForCurrentUser. LaunchctlControl's source was not supplied, so I could not verify how it resolves the home directory: HOME env, getpwuid, or the console user under sudo. The plist and log are user-owned files under the operator's own control (TB-003/ADV-001 already has full local access), so this is not a trust-escalation path. A future pass should still confirm that a root or sudo invocation cannot write the LaunchAgent plist or log into another user's home with root ownership. It should also confirm that the resolution matches the path WatchdogAgent (T-043) uses.

(2) restartAfterDrain (head lines ~166-187) now polls isLoaded() for up to 60s after bootout before bootstrap. This avoids a launchd error-5 race that left the provider unloaded. After the timeout it still calls loadService(), as before. It does not alter the stop/disable fencing or the kickstartIfLoaded watchdog semantics, and does not affect environment passthrough (inferencePassthroughEnvKeys, including DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE relevant to T-041). The impact is availability-only, and the change is positive.

No attestation, encryption, authorization, billing or data-exposure behavior changed. No findings qualify.
